s.dp: Physical Events and States › Sound
s.d: (derivative of ῥοῖζος ‘the noise made by something passing swiftly through the air,’ not occurring in the NT) pertaining to a sudden noise made by swift movement
s.g: with a shrill noise; with a rushing noise
s.c: The expression ‘with a rushing noise’ may be rendered as ‘suddenly and with a roar’ or ‘quickly and with a lot of noise.’

s.dp: Artifacts › Weapons and Armor
s.d: a large, broad sword used for both cutting and piercing
s.c: In a number of languages the term for ‘sword’ is simply ‘a large knife,’ but in some regions it may be called ‘a machete for killing.’

s.dp: Military Activities › To Fight
s.d: (figurative extension of meaning of {L:ῥομφαία<SDBG:ῥομφαία:000000>}[a] ‘broad sword,’ {D:6.32})
s.c: It is possible that ῥομφαία in ⟦Revelation 6:8|Revelation 6:8⟧ should be understood in its literal meaning of ‘broad sword’ (see LN 6.32).

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Sorrow, Regret
s.d: (an idiom, literally: a sword goes through one’s soul) to feel the intense pain of sorrow
s.g: to feel pain and sorrow; to be sorrowful and distressed

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: the oldest son of Jacob and ancestor of an Israelite tribe

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: the wife of Boaz in the genealogy of Jesus

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a son of Σίμων[d] of Cyrene

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a person greeted in {S:04501601300004}

s.dp: Geographical Objects and Features › Thoroughfares: Roads, Streets, Paths, etc.
s.d: a city thoroughfare which is relatively narrow

s.dp: Danger, Risk, Safe, Save › Cause To Be Safe, Free from Danger
s.d: to rescue from danger, with the implication that the danger in question is severe and acute

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Impurity
s.d: to live in a degenerate manner
s.g: to live in moral filth; to live a completely bad life

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Impurity
s.d: a state of moral impurity and filth

s.dp: Features of Objects › Clean, Dirty
s.d: pertaining to being dirty or filthy
s.c: In ⟦James 2:2|James 2:2⟧ the emphasis of ῥυπαρός is not upon clothes being ragged as one might expect in the case of a poor man, but upon the clothes being filthy and thus the basis for greater offense and avoidance.

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Impurity
s.d: pertaining to being morally impure or filthy
s.g: morally impure; morally filthy; morally perverted
s.c: It would be a mistake to assume that physical filth is necessarily related to moral impurity. Hence, one cannot simply take a word meaning ‘dirty’ and presume that it may carry the figurative significance of moral depravity or impurity. The equivalent in some languages is ‘moral degenerate,’ ‘stained with badness,’ ‘spotted with evil,’ or ‘has sin on him like leprous spots.’

s.dp: Features of Objects › Clean, Dirty
s.d: dirt as refuse in contrast with soil

s.dp: Physical Events and States › Events Involving Liquids and Dry Masses
s.d: the movement of a liquid in some direction{N:001}
s.c: In a number of languages a term referring to the flow of liquid may also be applied to the movement of any object, so that a literal rendering might be ‘the liquid moved.’ However, terms for ‘flow’ or ‘pour’ often differ substantially on the basis of the direction of the flow. For example, if the flow is relatively horizontal, and therefore slow, it may have one term, while if it is quite fast, another expression may be used, and if the flow is almost perpendicular (as in the case of pouring), a still different term is employed.

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Sickness, Disease, Weakness
s.d: (a set phrase, literally: flow of blood) the loss of blood through menstrual bleeding{N:002}
s.g: loss of blood; menstrual flow; bleeding

s.dp: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products › Parts of the Body
s.d: lines or creases in the skin{N:001}
s.c: In ⟦Ephesians 5:27|Ephesians 5:27⟧ ῥυτίς is used symbolically as a type of imperfection, but in some languages wrinkles can be an evidence of age and therefore of seniority and even wisdom

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: (derivative of Ρώμη ‘Rome,’ {D:93.563}) a person who lives in or is a native of Rome or a citizen of the Roman Empire

s.dp: Communication › Language
s.d: in the Latin language

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: the capital city of the Roman Empire

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Health, Vigor, Strength
s.d: (derivative of a base meaning literally ‘to be strong,’ ‘to be well,’ but used in the NT only as a formula for the ending of letters) to be well and to fare well{N:001}
s.c: The occurrence of ῥώννυμαι as an epistolary formula may be understood in two different senses: either as a sincere expression of the wish that the person involved may fare well or merely as a device to indicate that the letter is complete. This second sense of ῥώννυμαι is treated in LN 33.24.

s.dp: Communication › Discourse Types
s.d: to end a letter by means of the expression ἔρρωσθε (ἐρρώσσω in some manuscripts), always having a favorable connotation
s.c: Since in ⟦Acts 15:29|Acts 15:29⟧ ἔρρωσθε ends a letter, it may be necessary in some languages to employ a typical letter-ending formula which will at the same time be favorable, for example, ‘with best wishes’ or ‘with sincere greetings.’ It would be quite wrong to use literally an expression such as ‘goodbye’ if this would be employed only or principally in direct address rather than at the end of a letter. For another interpretation of ἔρρωσθε in ⟦Acts 15:29|Acts 15:29⟧, see LN 23.133.

s.dp: Help, Care For › Desert, Forsake
s.d: an Aramaic word meaning: you have forsaken me
s.c: Languages differ appreciably in expressions meaning ‘to forsake, to abandon.’ For example, the most appropriate equivalent in some instances is ‘to leave alone’ or ‘to leave behind.’ In other instances one may employ a phrase such as ‘to leave without help’ or ‘to leave and refuse to care for.’

s.dp: Supernatural Beings and Powers › Supernatural Beings
s.d: (a Greek transliteration of a Hebrew word meaning armies and used with {L:κύριος<SDBG:κύριος:000000>}[a] Lord, {D:12.9}, as a title for God) pertaining to one who has overwhelming power
s.g: Almighty; All Powerful; One who is powerful over all

s.dp: Time › Definite Units of Time: Year, Month, Week, Day, Hour
s.d: (derivative of {L:σάββατον<SDBG:σάββατον:000000>}[a], {D:67.184}) a special religiously significant period for rest and worship
s.g: a Sabbath rest; a period of rest

s.dp: Time › Definite Units of Time: Year, Month, Week, Day, Hour
s.d: the seventh or last day of the week (religiously the most important since it was consecrated to the worship of God)

s.dp: Time › Definite Units of Time: Year, Month, Week, Day, Hour
s.d: a period of seven days
s.c: In some languages it may be better to render ⟦Luke 18:12|Luke 18:12⟧ as simply ‘for every seven days, I fast two days.’ For the expression ‘the first day of the week,’ there may be a number of complications, especially since in present-day usage Monday is often regarded as ‘the first day of the week.’ For the NT, of course, the Sabbath Day, or ‘Saturday,’ marked the seventh day of the week and the next day would be regarded as ‘the first day of the week,’ namely, Sunday.

s.dp: Spacial Dimensions › Specific Measures of Length
s.d: a Sabbath day’s journey, somewhat over half a mile and about one kilometer
s.g: half a mile; one kilometer; Sabbath journey

s.dp: Artifacts › Instruments Used in Fishing
s.d: a long seine net used in fishing
s.c: The σαγήνη was a long net hanging vertically in the water with floats at the upper edge and weights at the lower. It was drawn in by men working in boats or from shore. In ⟦Matthew 13:47|Matthew 13:47⟧ the actual form of the net is not so important. What is significant is that the net was sufficiently large to catch a large number of different kinds of fish.

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › Socio-Religious
s.d: a member of a politically influential Jewish party in Jerusalem at the time of Jesus and the apostles. The Sadducees were a smaller group than the Pharisees (see {D:11.49}), but were often in control of important political and religious positions. Their denial of the resurrection of the dead and their acceptance of only the first five books of the OT are important elements in some of the important differences which arose between the Sadducees and the Pharisees

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a person in the genealogy of Jesus

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Change an Opinion Concerning Truth
s.d: to be so emotionally disturbed as to give up one’s beliefs
s.g: to give up one’s beliefs; shaken in one’s beliefs; to turn back from one’s beliefs

s.dp: Artifacts › Cloth, Leather, and Objects Made of Such Materials
s.d: a heavy material normally used for making sacks, but worn by persons in mourning and as a sign of repentance
s.c: In most languages sackcloth is described as ‘coarse cloth’ and sometimes as ‘heavy cloth.’

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: the father of Boaz in the genealogy of Jesus

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: the father of Eber in the genealogy of Jesus

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a person in the genealogy of Jesus ({S:04000100400030}; {S:04200303200017}, apparatus)

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a person in the genealogy of Jesus

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: a city on the southeast coast of Cyprus

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: a place in northern Samaria (location uncertain)

s.dp: Non-Linear Movement
s.d: to cause something to move back and forth rapidly, often violently
s.c: In some languages there are quite distinct terms for shaking, depending upon the vigor of the motion and/or the objects which are shaken. Accordingly, one must exercise care in selecting terms which will accurately and adequately represent the nature of the shaking in the various contexts. For example, in ⟦Hebrews 12:26|Hebrews 12:26⟧ the shaking would presumably involve some kind of reverberation, but in ⟦Revelation 6:13|Revelation 6:13⟧ the action of the wind suggests whipping something back and forth.|It is possible to interpret σαλεύω in ⟦Matthew 24:29|Matthew 24:29⟧ (αἱ δυνάμεις τῶν οὐρανῶν σαλευθήσονται ‘the hosts of heaven will be shaken’) as meaning literal shaking, but it may be used figuratively in the sense of deposing the hosts of heaven from their positions of power.

s.dp: Hostility, Strife › Riot
s.d: to cause people to riot against
s.g: to stir up against; to start a riot; to cause an uproar

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Worry, Anxiety, Distress, Peace
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:σαλεύω<SDBG:σαλεύω:000000>} ‘to shake,’ {D:16.7}) to become emotionally unsettled and distraught
s.g: to become unsettled; to be deeply distressed; to be upset

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: a place of which Melchizedek was king; see also {D:93.321}

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: the expression βασιλεὺς Σαλήμ ‘king of Salem’ ({S:05800700100012 05800700200034} may be interpreted as ‘king of peace,’ and as such it may be regarded as an honorific name
s.c: It is also possible that Σαλήμ refers to a place (see LN 93.566).

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: a promontory on the northeast corner of Crete

s.dp: Physical Events and States › Events Involving Liquids and Dry Masses
s.d: the tossing motion of large waves on a body of water

s.dp: Artifacts › Musical Instruments
s.d: a musical wind instrument; made of metal; frequently used in signaling, especially in connection with war
s.c: The present-day equivalent of the σάλπιγξ is the bugle.

s.dp: Artifacts › Musical Instruments
s.d: (derivative of {L:σαλπίζω<SDBG:σαλπίζω:000000>}[a] ‘to play the trumpet,’ {D:6.90}) the sound made by a trumpet{N:001}
s.c: With both σαλπίζω (LN 6.92) and σάλπιγξ, it may be necessary to introduce an agent, even though indefinite. For example, ἐν τῇ ἐσχάτω σάλπιγγι may be translated as ‘when someone blows the trumpet for the last time,’ and σαλπίσει may be rendered as ‘when someone sounds the trumpet’ or ‘when someone produces a noise on the trumpet.’ However, any term for ‘noise’ should imply a meaningful sound.

s.dp: Artifacts › Musical Instruments
s.d: (derivative of {L:σάλπιγξ<SDBG:σάλπιγξ:000000>}[a] trumpet, {D:6.89}) to produce sound with a trumpet
s.c: It is possible, of course, in ⟦Matthew 6:2|Matthew 6:2⟧ to interpret σαλπίζω as a type of causative and thus to say ‘to cause someone to blow the trumpet’ or ‘to have the trumpet blown.’

s.dp: Artifacts › Musical Instruments
s.d: to produce the sound of a trumpet (without specification of an agent)
s.g: to sound a trumpet; a trumpet sounds
s.c: In a number of languages it may be best to render σαλπίσει in ⟦1 Corinthians 15:52|1 Corinthians 15:52⟧ as ‘people will hear the sound of the trumpet’ or ‘the sound of the trumpet will be heard.’

s.dp: Artifacts › Musical Instruments
s.d: (derivative of {L:σαλπίζω<SDBG:σαλπίζω:000000>}[a] ‘to play the trumpet,’ {D:6.90}) one who plays the trumpet

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a Galilean woman who followed Jesus

s.d: a region in the central part of Palestine

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: the principal city of Samaria

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: (derivative of {L:Σαμάρεια<SDBG:Σαμάρεια:000000>} ‘Samaria,’ {D:93.568}) a person who is a native of Samaria

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: (derivative of {L:Σαμάρεια<SDBG:Σαμάρεια:000000>} ‘Samaria,’ {D:93.568}) a woman who is a native of Samaria

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: an island in the northern Aegean Sea

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: an island off the west coast of Asia Minor

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a major OT prophet

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: one of the judges of Israel

s.dp: Artifacts › Cloth, Leather, and Objects Made of Such Materials
s.d: a type of footwear consisting of a sole made of leather (or possibly wood) tied to the foot by means of thongs or straps

s.dp: Constructions › Building Materials
s.d: large board or plank of wood

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: the Hebrew name of the apostle Paul

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: the first king of Israel

s.dp: Value › Good, Bad
s.d: pertaining to being of poor or bad quality and hence of little or no value (particularly in reference to plants, either in the sense of seriously diseased or of seedling stock, that is, not budded or grafted)
s.c: Some scholars have suggested that σαπρός in ⟦Matthew 7:18|Matthew 7:18⟧ really refers to a seedling, that is to say, a tree which has grown up completely from seed rather than being budded or grafted. Seedling trees often produce tasteless or even bitter fruit. By its very nature, such a tree cannot produce good fruit and is, therefore, considered to be of no value.

s.dp: Violence, Harm, Destroy, Kill › Harm, Wound
s.d: pertaining to that which is harmful in view of its being unwholesome and corrupting
s.c: In ⟦Ephesians 4:29|Ephesians 4:29⟧ σαπρός is in contrast with that which is ἀγαθός ‘good’ for building up what is necessary. In such a context ἀγαθός may be interpreted as that which is helpful, and by contrast σαπρός may be understood to mean ‘harmful.’

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: the wife of Ἀνανίας 1

s.dp: Natural Substances › Precious and Semiprecious Stones and Substances
s.d: sapphire, usually blue in color (see {D:2.29})

s.dp: Artifacts › Containers
s.d: a large container made of woven material, usually grass or reeds; used for carrying a variety of things, including food and produce, and for moving soil from one place to another{N:001}
s.c: In the one context in which σαργάνη occurs (⟦2 Corinthians 11:33|2 Corinthians 11:33⟧), the basket was evidently rather large, since it was used to let Paul down from an opening in the wall of Damascus. It may very well have been made of braided ropes. In ⟦2 Corinthians 11:33|2 Corinthians 11:33⟧ the basket is called σαργάνη, while in ⟦Acts 9:25|Acts 9:25⟧ the same basket is referred to as σπυρίς ({D:6.149).

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: a city in western Asia Minor

s.dp: Natural Substances › Precious and Semiprecious Stones and Substances
s.d: carnelian or cornelian, usually red in color (see {D:2.29})

s.dp: Natural Substances › Precious and Semiprecious Stones and Substances
s.d: onyx, sardonyx, of varying colors (see {D:2.29})

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: a city on the coast of Phoenicia between Tyre and Sidon

s.dp: Psychological Faculties
s.d: pertaining to what is human or characteristic of human nature

s.dp: Features of Objects › Physical [Material], Spiritual
s.d: pertaining to being material or physical, with the possible implication of inferior
s.c: It is possible that σαρκικός in ⟦Romans 15:27|Romans 15:27⟧ refers to blessings for the body, but the context would seem to imply blessings of greater significance than those designed only for a person’s body.

s.dp: Features of Objects › Natural [Human], Spiritual
s.d: pertaining to the natural, physical characteristics of persons and often including their characteristic behavior{N:001}

s.dp: Behavior and Related States › Particular Patterns of Behavior
s.d: (derivative of {L:σάρξ<SDBG:σάρξ:000005>}[f] ‘human nature,’ {D:26.7}) pertaining to behavior which is typical of human nature, but with special focus upon more base physical desires
s.c: In some languages the expression τῶν σαρκικῶν ἐπιθυμιῶν in ⟦1 Peter 2:11|1 Peter 2:11⟧ may be rendered as ‘the desires which one’s body has’ or ‘what the body wants.’

s.dp: People › Human Beings
s.d: (derivative of {L:σάρξ<SDBG:σάρξ:000002>}[c] ‘people,’ {D:9.11}) pertaining to physical human beings
s.c: In ⟦Hebrews 7:16|Hebrews 7:16⟧ the phrase ‘human regulations’ can be rendered as ‘regulations made by people.’ For another interpretation of σάρκινος in ⟦Hebrews 7:16|Hebrews 7:16⟧, see LN 26.8.

s.dp: Psychological Faculties
s.d: pertaining to what is human or characteristic of human nature
s.c: For another interpretation of σάρκινος in ⟦Hebrews 7:16|Hebrews 7:16⟧, see LN 9.13.

s.dp: Features of Objects › Natural [Human], Spiritual
s.d: pertaining to the natural, physical characteristics of persons and often including their characteristic behavior{N:001}
s.c: For another interpretation of σάρκινος in ⟦1 Corinthians 3:1|1 Corinthians 3:1⟧, see LN 41.42.

s.dp: Behavior and Related States › Particular Patterns of Behavior
s.d: (derivative of {L:σάρξ<SDBG:σάρξ:000005>}[f] ‘human nature,’ {D:26.7}) pertaining to behavior which is typical of human nature, but with special focus upon more base physical desires
s.c: For another interpretation of σάρκινος in ⟦1 Corinthians 3:1|1 Corinthians 3:1⟧, see LN 79.4.

s.dp: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products › Parts of the Body
s.d: the flesh of both animals and human beings
s.c: Some languages make an important distinction between the flesh of a living person and the flesh of someone who has been killed or who has died. It would be this latter sense which should be reflected in ⟦Revelation 19:18|Revelation 19:18⟧. In ⟦Romans 2:28|Romans 2:28⟧ the reference to ‘circumcision in the flesh’ (ἐν σαρκὶ περιτομή) would, however, require the first sense, namely, the flesh of a living person.

s.dp: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products › Body
s.d: a living body{N:001}
s.c: Though the reference of σάρξ in ⟦1 Timothy 3:16|1 Timothy 3:16⟧ is to the physical body, it may be necessary in some instances to translate this as ‘a human being’ or ‘a person,’ that is to say, ‘Christ appeared as a human being’ or ‘Christ became a person.’ Otherwise, the reader might assume that Christ took on the body of someone else or merely indwelt some miraculous human form rather than actually became a human being

s.dp: People › Human Beings
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:σάρξ<SDBG:σάρξ:000000>}[a] ‘flesh,’ {D:8.63}) humans as physical beings

s.dp: People › Human Beings
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:σάρξ<SDBG:σάρξ:000000>}[a] ‘flesh,’ {D:8.63}) human nature, with emphasis upon the physical aspects
s.c: In a number of languages it would seem strange, if not totally redundant, to speak of ‘physical fathers’ or ‘human fathers’ (⟦Hebrews 12:9|Hebrews 12:9⟧), since the term ‘fathers’ would suffice, and any addition would be misleading. In some instances, however, one might use an expression such as ‘our own fathers,’ so as to provide an implied contrast with the heavenly Father. Where it is necessary to qualify the term ‘fathers,’ one may use an expression such as ‘fathers which caused us to be conceived.’

s.dp: Kinship Terms › Groups and Members of Groups of Persons Regarded as Related by Blood but without Special Reference to Successive Generations
s.d: a relatively large group of persons regarded as being biologically related{N:002}
s.c: It may be difficult in some languages to clearly distinguish between culture and race as in ⟦Mark 7:26|Mark 7:26⟧. Sometimes this difference can be indicated by saying ‘the woman lived like a Greek, but she was a Syrophoenician’ or ‘… her parents were from Syrophoenicia.’ In translating ‘people of my own race’ in ⟦Romans 11:14|Romans 11:14⟧, it may be necessary to say ‘all my fellow Jews’ or ‘all those people of whom I am a part’ or ‘those people who are my roots’ or ‘… my trunk,’ based on the analogy of a tree trunk and branches.

s.dp: Psychological Faculties
s.d: the psychological aspect of human nature which contrasts with the spiritual nature; in other words, that aspect of human nature which is characterized by or reflects typical human reasoning and desires in contrast with those aspects of human thought and behavior which relate to God and the spiritual life
s.g: human nature; human aspects; natural; human
s.c: Some scholars understand the meaning of σάρξ as being a person’s lower nature rather than simply human nature, but the distinction between lower nature and higher nature seems to be primarily one arising out of typical Greek thought rather than out of the Semitic background which seems to be so pervasive in the use of the term σάρξ in NT contexts such as ⟦1 Corinthians 1:26|1 Corinthians 1:26⟧. There are, of course, contexts in which σάρξ does refer to that psychological factor in man which serves as a willing instrument of sin and is subject to sin.

s.dp: Nature, Class, Example › Nature, Character
s.d: human nature, particularly in reference to the physical aspect of human life
s.g: human nature; physical nature of people
s.c: In some languages one may more appropriately translate this phrase in ⟦Galatians 4:23|Galatians 4:23⟧ as ‘was born like any person is’ or ‘was born like people are normally born.’

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Live, Die
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:σάρξ<SDBG:σάρξ:000000>}[a] ‘flesh,’ {D:8.63}) physical life

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Desire Strongly
s.d: (an idiom, literally: desire of the flesh) desire for sexual gratification

s.dp: People › Human Beings
s.d: (an idiom, literally: flesh and blood) a human being in contrast with a divine being{N:003}

s.dp: Trouble, Hardship, Relief, Favorable Circumstances › Experience Trouble, Hardship
s.d: (an idiom, literally: thorn in the flesh) something which causes serious trouble and difficulty
s.g: trouble; woe; suffering; serious inconvenience; thorn in the flesh
s.c: There are a number of different interpretations of σκόλοψ τῇ σαρκί in ⟦2 Corinthians 12:7|2 Corinthians 12:7⟧ (see discussion at LN 20.27).

s.dp: Household Activities
s.d: to sweep by using a broom

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: the wife of Abraham

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: the plain along the coast of Palestine

s.dp: Supernatural Beings and Powers › Supernatural Beings
s.d: (a borrowing from Hebrew and Aramaic: a title for the Devil, literally: adversary) the principal supernatural evil being{N:001}
s.c: In a number of languages there is a well known proper name for the Devil as the chief of all demons. In other instances, however, he is given a descriptive name, for example, ‘the ruler of the evil spirits,’ ‘the chief of the demons,’ ‘the truly bad one,’ ‘the left-handed one’ (as the one who is opposed to all which is right or correct), ‘the no-good one,’ ‘the avaricious one.’ In some instances a term for the Devil may be highly idiomatic as, for example, ‘the barking one,’ a reference to the Devil’s presumed activity in animal guise.|Some translators have employed for ‘Devil’ the proper name Satan, but this is often not a satisfactory solution. In one language in West Africa, for example, the term Satan had already been borrowed but was understood in the sense of the culture hero of the people and not as a designation for the chief of demons.|See also ⟦Revelation 20:2|Revelation 20:2⟧.

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: (a borrowing from Hebrew and Aramaic meaning literally: adversary) the usual proper name of the Devil; see also {D:12.34}

s.dp: Spacial Dimensions › Specific Measures of Volume
s.d: the Hebrew measure for grain, about a peck and a half or somewhat less than one-half bushel (a bushel consists of four pecks) or approximately twelve liters in the metric system
s.c: In ⟦Matthew 13:33|Matthew 13:33⟧ the precise amount of flour is not important. What is important is to provide some type of measurement which will indicate a considerable quantity.

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: an alternative form of {L:Σαούλ<SDBG:Σαούλ:000000>}, {D:93.327}, the Hebrew name of the apostle Paul

s.dp: Physical Events and States › Burning
s.d: to cause a fire to be extinguished
s.g: to extinguish a fire; to put out a fire
s.c: ‘To put out fierce fires’ may be expressed as ‘to cause fierce fires no longer to burn’ or ‘to make large fires stop burning.’ In order to speak of ‘fierce fires’ it may be necessary in some languages to speak of ‘large, hot fires.’

s.dp: Aspect › Cease, Stop
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:σβέννυμι<SDBG:σβέννυμι:000000>}[a] ‘to extinguish a fire,’ {D:14.70}) to cause a fervent activity to cease
s.c: Though the particular activity of the Spirit is not overtly indicated in the context of ⟦1 Thessalonians 5:19|1 Thessalonians 5:19⟧, the book as a whole contains sufficient reference to the activity of the Spirit so as to indicate what is involved.

s.dp: Physical Events and States › Burning
s.d: to cease burning, either because of lack of material to be burned or because the fire has been forcibly extinguished
s.c: The expression ‘our lamps are going out’ may be rendered as ‘our lamps will soon not be burning’ or ‘our lamps will burn only a little bit more.’ It may, however, be misleading to speak of ‘lamps burning’ (see discussion in LN 14.65), and accordingly, it may be much better to translate ‘our lamps will show light only a little bit more’ or ‘the oil in our lamps will burn only a little bit more.’

s.dp: Discourse Referentials › Receptor, Receptors
s.d: a reflexive reference to a receptor noted in the immediate context
s.c: For the plural, see LN 92.25.

s.dp: Religious Activities › Worship, Reverence
s.d: to express in attitude and ritual one’s allegiance to and regard for deity
s.c: In a number of languages worship is expressed in an idiomatic manner, for example, ‘to bow down before,’ ‘to lower one’s head before,’ ‘to raise one’s arms to,’ ‘to sing to,’ ‘to honor.’ It is important in selecting an expression for worship to employ a term or phrase which will include various aspects of worship.

s.dp: Religious Activities › Worship, Reverence
s.d: (derivative of {L:σεβάζομαι<SDBG:σεβάζομαι:000000>} ‘to worship,’ {D:53.53}) a place of worship
s.c: For another interpretation of σέβασμα in ⟦Acts 17:23|Acts 17:23⟧, see LN 53.55.

s.dp: Religious Activities › Worship, Reverence
s.d: (derivative of {L:σεβάζομαι<SDBG:σεβάζομαι:000000>} ‘to worship,’ {D:53.53}) an object which is worshiped
s.c: For another interpretation of σέβασμα in ⟦Acts 17:23|Acts 17:23⟧, see LN 53.54.

s.dp: Control, Rule › Rule, Govern
s.d: (derivative of ὁ {L:Σεβαστός<SDBG:σεβαστός>} ‘the Emperor,’ {D:37.75}) pertaining to the Emperor
s.c: The phrase ‘the imperial regiment’ may be rendered as ‘the group of soldiers who protected the Emperor’ or ‘… who were under the direct command of the Emperor.’

s.dp: Control, Rule › Rule, Govern
s.d: (derivative of σεβαστός ‘revered, worthy of reverence,’ not occurring in the NT) a title for the Roman Emperor and denoting his semidivine status

s.dp: Religious Activities › Worship, Reverence
s.d: to express in attitude and ritual one’s allegiance to and regard for deity
s.c: In a number of languages worship is expressed in an idiomatic manner, for example, ‘to bow down before,’ ‘to lower one’s head before,’ ‘to raise one’s arms to,’ ‘to sing to,’ ‘to honor.’ It is important in selecting an expression for worship to employ a term or phrase which will include various aspects of worship.

s.dp: Artifacts › Instruments Used in Binding and Fastening
s.d: a pliable instrument of binding
s.g: chain (made of metal) or rope (made of fiber)
s.c: In a number of languages a term for chain is simply metal rope. In other languages it may be described as linked rope in contrast with twisted rope, that is, a rope made out of some kind of fiber.|The phrase σειραῖς ζόφου (⟦2 Peter 2:4|2 Peter 2:4⟧) is admittedly a strange expression, and in some manuscripts this gave rise to a slight change in orthography (σιροῖς; see LN 1.59) with the resulting meaning being ‘in pits of darkness.’ If, however, one adopts the text ἀλλὰ σειραῖς ζόφου ταρταρώσας, it may be possible to interpret the entire expression as ‘but he chained them in the darkness of hell.’

s.dp: Physical Events and States › Movement of the Earth
s.d: a sudden and severe movement of the earth
s.c: Since earthquakes are universal in occurrence, there is normally no difficulty involved in finding some way of speaking about them. However, in a number of languages idiomatic expressions are used, for example, ‘the devil rolled over’ or ‘mother earth belched.’|In ⟦Acts 16:26|Acts 16:26⟧ the earthquake is regarded as the cause of the prison foundations shaking, and it may be better to restructure the relationships expressed in ⟦Acts 16:26|Acts 16:26⟧ as ‘the prison shook because of the earthquake.’

s.dp: Physical Events and States › Events Involving Liquids and Dry Masses
s.d: a violent action of the surface of a body of water as the result of high waves caused by a strong wind
s.c: Though the term σεισμός obviously implies the strong action of the wind, the focus is upon the violent motion caused by the waves. It might, therefore, be more appropriate to translate ⟦Matthew 8:24|Matthew 8:24⟧ as ‘there were huge waves on the sea’ or ‘… on the lake.’ Such a translation would then be appropriate for the following clause.

s.dp: Non-Linear Movement
s.d: to cause something to move back and forth rapidly, often violently
s.c: In some languages there are quite distinct terms for shaking, depending upon the vigor of the motion and/or the objects which are shaken. Accordingly, one must exercise care in selecting terms which will accurately and adequately represent the nature of the shaking in the various contexts. For example, in ⟦Hebrews 12:26|Hebrews 12:26⟧ the shaking would presumably involve some kind of reverberation, but in ⟦Revelation 6:13|Revelation 6:13⟧ the action of the wind suggests whipping something back and forth.

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Worry, Anxiety, Distress, Peace
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:σείω<SDBG:σείω:000000>}[a] ‘to shake,’ {D:16.7}) to cause extreme anxiety and apprehension, implying accompanying movement
s.g: to stir up; to cause an uproar; to cause great anxiety

s.dp: Non-Linear Movement
s.d: to shake or tremble, often with the implication of fear and/or consternation
s.g: to tremble; trembling; to quiver; to shake
s.c: In a number of languages there are two distinct terms for trembling, one relating to illness (as in the case of epileptic seizures or the chills and fever associated with malaria) and the other associated with fear.

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a Christian of Thessalonica who was a companion of Paul

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: the port city of Antioch in Syria

s.dp: Geographical Objects and Features › Heavenly Bodies
s.d: a celestial body smaller than the sun that gives light to earth in the nighttime; the moon’s appearance changes over the course of each month as the angle we can see the moon’s half-illuminated surface changes
s.c: As in the case of ἥλιος the sun (LN 1.28), there are relatively few difficulties involved in obtaining a satisfactory word for σελήνη ‘the moon,’ though there may also be a tendency to add some kind of honorific or title, for example, ‘mother moon.’ At the same time, certain difficulties may occur in some passages. For example, in ⟦Luke 21:25|Luke 21:25⟧ it may be misleading to speak of signs occurring ‘in the moon,’ for this might mean ‘inside the moon.’ TEV has resolved the problem somewhat by translating “there will be strange things happening to the sun, the moon, and the stars.” One may also translate ‘the sun, the moon, and the stars will cause signs in the heavens’ or ‘… portents in the sky.’

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Sickness, Disease, Weakness
s.d: to suffer epileptic seizures (associated in ancient times with the supernatural power of the moon)
s.g: to suffer epileptic seizures; to be an epileptic

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a person in the genealogy of Jesus

s.dp: Foods and Condiments › Food
s.d: a fine grade of wheat flour

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Modesty, Propriety
s.d: pertaining to appropriate, befitting behavior and implying dignity and respect
s.g: honorable; worthy of respect; of good character

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Modesty, Propriety
s.d: behavior which is befitting, implying a measure of dignity leading to respect
s.c: In some languages ‘propriety’ is best expressed as ‘to act in the right way’ or ‘to act as one ought.’

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: Sergius Paulus, the governor of Cyprus

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a person in the genealogy of Jesus

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a person in the genealogy of Jesus

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a person in the genealogy of Jesus

s.dp: Communication › Interpret, Mean, Explain
s.d: to cause something to be both specific and clear
s.g: to indicate clearly; to make clear

s.dp: Communication › Non-Verbal Communication
s.d: an event which is regarded as having some special meaning
s.c: In translating σημεῖον in ⟦Matthew 24:3|Matthew 24:3⟧, it may be necessary in some languages to say ‘tell us what will happen that will show that you are coming’ or ‘tell us what we will see that will make us know that you are coming.’|σημεῖον as an event with special meaning was inevitably an unusual or even miraculous type of occurrence, and in a number of contexts σημεῖον may be rendered as ‘miracle.’ Certainly that is the referent of the term σημεῖον in ⟦John 2:23|John 2:23⟧ (πολλοὶ ἐπίστευσαν εἰς τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦθεωροῦντες αὐτοῦ τὰ σημεῖα ἅ ἐποίει ‘many believed in him as they saw the signs he did’). For the Gospel of John, however, a σημεῖον is not simply a miraculous event but something which points to a reality with even greater significance. A strictly literal translation of σημεῖον as ‘sign’ might mean nothing more than a road sign or a sign on a building, and therefore in some languages σημεῖον in a context such as ⟦John 2:23|John 2:23⟧ may be rendered as ‘a miracle with great meaning.’

s.dp: Memory and Recall › Storing of Information
s.d: to pay special attention to something for the sake of a future recall and response
s.g: to take note of; to pay special attention to

s.dp: Time › Units of Time with Reference to Other Units or Points of Time: Yesterday, Today, Next Day
s.d: the same day as the day of a discourse

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Rot, Decay
s.d: to rot or decay, in reference to organic matter
s.c: There may be problems involved in a literal rendering of ⟦James 5:2|James 5:2⟧ because it may seem strange to speak of ‘riches rotting,’ since a term for ‘riches’ is likely to refer primarily to money. It may therefore be necessary to translate ‘the things that make you rich’ or ‘all the things you have as a rich person.’

s.dp: Animals › Insects
s.d: smallish brown or gray moth that lays eggs in clothing or other cloth; eggs hatch into very small caterpillars, which feed on the fibers; Tineidae family, probably Tineola biselliella; symbols of decay, ruin, and slow destruction
s.c: In the NT the Greek term σής is used only in reference to the larvae of moths, and therefore it is frequently necessary to employ a term in the receptor language for the larvae rather than for the flying insect. This means that frequently an appropriate equivalent is ‘the worms of moths,’ but often one can employ an expression which means simply ‘cloth worms’ or ‘cloth eaters.’|In ⟦Matthew 6:19|Matthew 6:19⟧, ⟦Matthew 6:20|Matthew 6:20⟧, ⟦Luke 12:33|Luke 12:33⟧ the effect of the larvae of moths is combined with rust as agents for the destruction of valuable objects. It is rare, however, that one can speak of the destruction caused by moths in the same way as one can describe the effects of rust or tarnish. It may therefore be necessary to talk about ‘moths eating cloth,’ while ‘tarnish ruins precious metal.’

s.dp: Violence, Harm, Destroy, Kill › Harm, Wound
s.d: pertaining to that which has been damaged by the larvae of moths
s.c: This expression in ⟦James 5:2|James 5:2⟧ may often be rendered as ‘your garments have been eaten by worms’ or ‘your garments are full of holes.’

s.dp: Able, Capable
s.d: to cause someone to be or to become more able or capable, with the implication of a contrast with weakness
s.g: to make more able; to strengthen
s.c: The terms στηρίζω (see LN 74.19) and σθενόω in ⟦1 Peter 5:10|1 Peter 5:10⟧ are very similar in meaning and serve primarily to intensify the meaning of making persons more able to engage in or to undergo certain experiences.

s.dp: Artifacts › Cloth, Leather, and Objects Made of Such Materials
s.d: fabric made of threads from the lustrous tough elastic fiber produced by silkworms for their cocoons; highly valued
